TOP: PHP2Shell RCE flaws hit every PHP since 5, exploited before disclosure
LiteLLM release poisoned on PyPI and Docker, steals cloud and SSH secrets
Railway urges all users to revoke secret keys after breach
GitLab patches critical unauthenticated code execution bug

P.h: PHP2Shell: two critical PHP remote code execution flaws, exploited since October 17
P.p: The flaws enable unauthenticated remote code execution. Exploitation attempts began on October 17, four days before PHP shipped fixes on October 21. Cisco, AWS, Google Cloud, Ubuntu, Debian and Palo Alto Networks issued patches or detections, and CISA, UK NCSC and CERT-EU urge immediate updates. Some European government, school and hospital sites went offline.
P.s: TLDR DevOps says proof-of-concept code is public and every PHP version from 5 onward is affected. Update to 8.2.35, 8.3.36, 8.4.27 or 8.5.12. There are no patches for PHP 8.1 or earlier. Amazon advises measuring mitigation in hours.

items.h: LiteLLM release poisoned on PyPI and Docker
items.d: Version 1.107.0 carried an infostealer and remote access trojan that ran when Python started. It took browser, AWS, Google Cloud, Azure, LLM API, SSH and GPG secrets. Anyone who ran it should rotate credentials.

items.h: Railway tells all users to revoke secret keys
items.d: Attackers accessed encrypted environment variables and decrypted some customer secrets, Railway says.
Stolen: email addresses, account creation dates, login counts and the latest login IP. A smaller number of accounts also had personal data leaked.

items.h: TiDB breach used stolen service-account credentials
items.d: PingCAP says attackers copied data and source code between September 9 and October 7. A group claims it also took API keys and SQL histories. Customer databases were reportedly untouched.

P.h: GitLab fixes critical bug that lets unauthenticated users run code
P.p: GitLab released patches for 12 issues. The worst is a critical integer overflow in its regular-expression compiler that lets an unauthenticated attacker execute arbitrary code on CE and EE servers. Fixes cover versions 18.11.13 through 19.5.1, and affected releases go back to 7.0. A second fix stops an OmniAuth SAML user taking over an LDAP-backed account.
P.s: GitLab says the patches include database migrations, so single-node installs may need downtime. Separately, TLDR DevOps reports private keys for eight eMudhra intermediate certificates were compromised on October 19, letting attackers forge certificates for any domain. Cloudflare has patched.

tiles.t: AWS key quarantine is not revocation
tiles.d: Truffle Security found the quarantine policy still allows reading Secrets Manager, Parameter Store and S3 object versions. Many leaked keys stayed exposed for years.

tiles.t: Backdoored models are easy to make
tiles.d: ProjectDiscovery fine-tuned Qwen2.5-7B to leak a .env file on a trigger phrase, using 20% poisoned prompts.
Device code phishing and redirect_uri abuse. Use admin consent and audit redirect URIs.

tiles.t: Entra ID ends native SMS MFA
tiles.d: Retired February 1, 2027, or July 1, 2027 for Global Administrators. Microsoft pushes passkeys.

tiles.t: 7 of 10 PQC libraries accept bad keys

P.h: Claude Duet and ServiceNow Arc: always-on agents ship with guardrails
P.p: Anthropic announced a research preview of Claude Duet, a proactive agent app for professionals and small businesses. Built on Claude Opus 5.5, it works in the background in a virtual machine with its own browser, sends daily briefs and monitors connected apps, with safety classifiers guarding sensitive data.
P.s: ServiceNow and Nvidia launched Arc, a long-running enterprise agent that runs locally on RTX Spark devices or in Nvidia OpenShell. Its control layers use Control Tower, OpenShell and AI Passport to enforce policy and manage agent permissions.

tiles.d: Backers include Tencent and CATL. It prepares a possible IPO while US restrictions grow.

tiles.t: OpenAI models come to Google Cloud
tiles.d: Model Garden and Codex, bought through the Marketplace. Microsoft stays primary partner.
Google Cloud A5X instances, plus rack-scale confidential computing planned.

tiles.t: GitHub rebuilds Git for AI agents
tiles.d: 99.99999% of repositories now have copies in Azure. Per-reference write coordination gave 3 to 4x throughput in tests.

P.h: GitHub Actions workflow lockfiles reach public preview
P.p: Lockfiles pin actions and their transitive dependencies to reviewed commits while keeping readable tags in workflow files. The preview includes a GitHub CLI extension to generate them, Dependabot support to update them, and policies that require workflows to use them.
P.s: Also from DevOps: Harness AI Budgets enforces weekly spend limits per team, developer, model or project and pauses access at 100%. Harness reports weekly AI spend per developer fell about 37% in its internal test.

tiles.d: Assistant Watchers reached general availability. Adaptive Telemetry customers report cutting spend 30% to 50%. Marketplace launched with 30+ plugins.
Radar: 86% of faults diagnosed within two minutes, versus 60% for a plain shell.
Akuity: 200+ clusters synced with no gate. Roll out in waves and halt on failed checks.
Big cascades hold locks and queue queries behind a migration. Soft delete, then clean up in bounded batches.

items.h: Three OpenAI safety researchers fired over Signal chats
items.d: Security officers found disappearing messages on personal devices. OpenAI cites sensitive-information policies. The researchers say it closes a channel to outside scrutiny.

items.h: The volunteer who patches PHP for most of the world
items.d: Ondřej Surý helped distributors fix the PHP flaws fast, paid only by donations. He discusses the AI-cybersecurity crisis.

items.h: curl: the slop is gone, the volume is not
items.d: Daniel Stenberg says hallucinated reports faded since spring 2026. Now maintainers face accurate but wordy AI reports they cannot ignore.

items.h: LLMs make formal verification feasible at scale
items.d: Models can now produce formal proofs at scale, enabling workflows with proven security guarantees.
